D001906.s: A disease caused by potent protein neurotoxins produced by clostridium botulinum which interfere with the presynaptic release of acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction.

D002424.s: Strong alkaline chemicals that destroy soft body tissues resulting in a deep, penetrating type of burn, in contrast to corrosives, that result in a more superficial type of damage via chemical means or inflammation. Caustics are usually hydroxides of light metals.

D002451.s: A partitioning within cells due to the selectively permeable membranes which enclose each of the separate parts, e.g., mitochondria, lysosomes, etc.

D002640.s: A postpartum condition consists of persistent lactation (galactorrhea) and amenorrhea in patients not breast feeding.

D002925.s: Conditions caused by abnormal cilia movement in the body, usually causing kartagener syndrome, chronic respiratory disorders, chronic sinusitis, and chronic otitis. Abnormal ciliary beating is likely due to defects in any of the 200 plus ciliary proteins, such as missing motor enzyme dynein arms.

D003535.s: An island republic in the eastern Mediterranean Sea. Its capital is Nicosia. It was colonized by the Phoenicians and ancient Greeks and ruled successively by the Assyrian, Persian, Ptolemaic, Roman, and Byzantine Empires.

D003742.s: Devices used in the home by persons to maintain dental and periodontal health. The devices include toothbrushes, dental flosses, water irrigators, gingival stimulators, etc.

D004035.s: Adjusting the quantity and quality of food intake to improve health status of an individual. This term does not include the methods of food intake (nutritional support).

D004242.s: An activity in which the organism plunges into water. It includes scuba and bell diving. Diving as natural behavior of animals goes here, as well as diving in decompression experiments with humans or animals.

D004512.s: Formal instruction, learning, or training in the preparation, dispensing, and proper utilization of drugs in the field of medicine.

D005726.s: Ganglia of the parasympathetic nervous system, including the ciliary, pterygopalatine, submandibular, and otic ganglia in the cranial region and intrinsic (terminal) ganglia associated with target organs in the thorax and abdomen.

D006213.s: Drugs capable of inducing illusions, hallucinations, delusions, paranoid ideations, and other alterations of mood and thinking.

D007492.s: A country bordering the Gulf of Oman, the Persian Gulf, and the Caspian Sea, between Iraq and Pakistan. The capital is Tehran.

D007566.s: A benign, autosomally recessive inherited hyperbilirubinemia characterized by the presence of a dark pigment in the centrilobular region of the liver cells. There is a functional defect in biliary excretion of bilirubin, cholephilic dyes, and porphyrins.

D007805.s: Conditions characterized by language abilities (comprehension and expression of speech and writing) that are below the expected level for a given age, generally in the absence of an intellectual impairment.

D008956.s: Theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of chemical processes or phenomena; includes the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electronic equipment.

D009010.s: In statistics, a technique for numerically approximating the solution of a mathematical problem by studying the distribution of some random variable, often generated by a computer.

D009087.s: Mucopolysaccharidosis with excessive chondroitin sulfate B in urine, characterized by dwarfism and deafness. It is caused by a deficiency of N-acetylgalactosamine-4-sulfatase (arylsulfatase B).

D009425.s: Animal behavior associated with the nest; includes construction, effects of size and material; behavior of the adult during the nesting period and the effect of the nest on the behavior of the young.

D009924.s: A technique for maintenance or growth of animal organs in vitro. It refers to three-dimensional cultures of undisaggregated tissue retaining some or all of the histological features of the tissue in vivo. (Freshney, Culture of Animal Cells, 3d ed, p1)

D010258.s: Behavior exhibited by individuals who are overly suspicious, but without the constellation of symptoms characteristic of paranoid personality disorder or paranoid type of schizophrenia.

D012032.s: The period of time following the triggering of an action potential when the cell membrane has changed to an unexcitable state and is gradually restored to the resting (excitable) state. During the absolute refractory period no other stimulus can trigger a response.

D012186.s: New abnormal growth of tissue in the retroperitoneal space.

D012591.s: An operation for retinal detachment which reduces the size of the globe by indenting the sclera so that it approximates the retina.

D013000.s: The biologic treatment of mental disorders (e.g., electroconvulsive therapy), in contrast with psychotherapy. (Stone, American Psychiatric Glossary, 1988, p159)

D013264.s: In horses, cattle, and other quadrupeds, the joint between the femur and the tibia, corresponding to the human knee.

D013659.n: Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act
e: United States Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act
D013659.s: PL97-248. Title II of the Act specifies provisions relating to savings in health and income security programs. This includes changes in payment for services, benefits and premiums of Medicare as well as changes in provisions under Medicaid and other specific programs covered by Social Security.

D013798.s: A gonadal stromal neoplasm composed only of theca cells, occurring mostly in the postmenopausal ovary.

D013927.s: Formation and development of a thrombus or blood clot in blood vessels.

D014067.s: Tumors or cancer of the palatine tonsil.

D014773.s: The study of the structure, growth, function, genetics, and reproduction of viruses, and virus diseases.

D016263.s: Renal syndrome in human immunodeficiency virus-infected patients characterized by nephrotic syndrome, severe proteinuria, focal and segmental glomerulosclerosis with distinctive tubular and interstitial changes, enlarged kidneys, and peculiar tubuloreticular structures.

D016380.s: Transference of brain tissue, either from a fetus or from a born individual, between individuals of the same species or between individuals of different species.

D016418.s: Work consisting of collections of law reports or the published reports of decided cases and documents or filings related to those cases.

D016533.s: Procedures for identifying types and strains of fungi.

D016850.s: An annular transitional zone, approximately 1 mm wide, between the cornea and the bulbar conjunctiva and sclera. It is highly vascular and is involved in the metabolism of the cornea.

D017758.s: The transmission of infectious disease or pathogens from patients to health professionals or health care workers. It includes transmission via direct or indirect exposure to bacterial, fungal, parasitic, or viral agents.

D018250.s: A rare cutaneous tumor of apocrine or eccrine sweat gland origin. It is most commonly found on the extremities and is usually benign. It appears as a solitary nodule or cyst and may be solid or produce a watery discharge.

D018434.s: A quality-of-life scale developed in the United States in 1972 as a measure of health status or dysfunction generated by a disease.

D018441.s: Encrustations formed from microbes (bacteria, algae, fungi, plankton, or protozoa) embedded in an extracellular polymeric substance matrix that is secreted by the microbes. They occur on body surfaces such as teeth (dental deposits); inanimate objects, and bodies of water.

D018889.s: A bone fixation technique using an external fixator (fixators, external) for lengthening limbs, correcting pseudarthroses and other deformities, and assisting the healing of otherwise hopeless traumatic or pathological fractures and infections, such as chronic osteomyelitis.

D018917.s: Ischemic injury to the optic nerve which usually affects the optic disk (optic neuropathy, anterior ischemic) and less frequently the retrobulbar portion of the nerve (optic neuropathy, posterior ischemic).

D018980.s: A disorder caused by hemizygous microdeletion of about 28 genes on chromosome 7q11.23, including the elastin gene. Clinical manifestations include supravalvular aortic stenosis; mental retardation; elfin facies; impaired visuospatial constructive abilities; and transient hypercalcemia in infancy.

D019028.s: A type of imaging technique used primarily in the field of cardiology. By coordinating the fast gradient-echo MRI sequence with retrospective ECG-gating, numerous short time frames evenly spaced in the cardiac cycle are produced.

D019723.s: Instruments for the visual examination of interior structures of the body. There are rigid endoscopes and flexible fiberoptic endoscopes for various types of viewing in endoscopy.

D019958.n: Attention Deficit and Disruptive Behavior Disorders
e: Attention Deficit and Disruptive Behavioral Disorders
D019958.s: Includes two similar disorders: oppositional defiant disorder and conduct disorders. Symptoms occurring in children with these disorders include: defiance of authority figures, angry outbursts, and other antisocial behaviors.

D022101.s: An amorphous region of electron dense material in the cytoplasm from which the microtubules polymerization is nucleated. The pericentriolar region of the centrosome which surrounds the centrioles is an example.

D032041.s: Genes whose entire sequences are contained within other genes.

D050377.s: The chilling of a tissue or organ during decreased blood perfusion or in the absence of blood supply.

D052256.s: Clinical syndrome describing overuse tendon injuries characterized by a combination of PAIN, diffuse or localized swelling, and impaired performance.

D054715.s: Agents that have a damaging effect on the heart. Such damage can occur from alkylating agents; free radicals; or metabolites from oxidative stress and in some cases is countered by cardiotonic agents.

D056304.s: An inward slant of the thigh in which the knees are close together and the ankles far apart. Genu valgum can develop due to skeletal and joint dysplasias (e.g., osteoarthritis; hurler syndrome); and malnutrition (e.g., rickets; fluoride poisoning).

D057219.s: Process by which unwanted microbial, plant or animal materials or organisms accumulate on man-made surfaces.

D058625.s: Final stage of a liver disease when the liver failure is irreversible and liver transplantation is needed.

D058849.s: Conformational transitions of a protein from unfolded states (after protein unfolding) to a more folded state.

D059006.s: Structures within the cell nucleus of insect cells containing DNA.

D066264.s: Subject matter related to the curation of data from research projects, stored permanently in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing.

D000066477.s: Measure of how well someone performs given tasks at their place of work.

D000067470.s: Procedures used for the induction of cellular reprogramming to change the terminal phenotype of a cell, such as the generation of induced pluripotent stem cells from differentiated adult cells by the forced expression of specific genes.

D000071059.s: Therapeutic use of bacteriophages to treat diseases.

D000071697.s: Skin lumpiness or skin surface dimpling often seen on the thighs, buttocks and abdomen. It is due to protrusion of subcutaneous fat into the dermis layer of skin.

D000075363.s: A nonproliferative disorder of plasma cells characterized by excessive production and misfolding of immunoglobulin light chains that form insoluble amyloid fibrils (see amyloid deposits) in various tissues.

D000078782.s: Branch of medicine concerned with the development of vaccines to control disease by identifying genetic and other mechanisms and pathways that determine immune responses, and thereby provide new candidate vaccine approaches.

D000082642.s: Measurements of the thickness of the cerebral cortex often detected automatically from medical imaging. Abnormal changes in cortical thickness (e.g., cortical thinning) are potential biomarkers for various neuropathologies.

D000091682.s: Differences in health status and in the distribution of health resources between different population groups, arising from the social conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work and age…

D000096382.s: Phenotypic changes of endothelial cells to mesenchyme type during development or during disease states such as inflammation; cancer; fibrosis or cardiovascular disease.

D000099057.s: A healthcare framework that typically integrates clinical information systems to improve clinical decision-making, support for community resources and SELF-management and improvement of care continuity through better delivery system design and organization.

D000099123.s: The altered pattern of gene expression related to rna methylation.
